title: The genitive, dative and ablative
deck: Three more cases, each with its own English: the genitive for "of", the dative for "to" or "for", and the ablative for "by", "with" or "from".
desc: GCSE Latin grammar, Chapter 2: the genitive, dative and ablative of 1st and 2nd declension nouns, what each means in English, with sentences to translate.
key: "of", or 's: domini, of the master, the master's
-ae, -o and -is each do more than one job

marks.c: the noun in the new case

blocks.lead: In Chapter 1 a noun was either the subject (nominative) or the object (accusative). Latin has three more cases, and each one carries a little English word with it: "of", "to" or "with". Find the case, and you know which word to add.

example.note: domini is genitive: "of the master", or "the master's". It belongs to pecuniam.

example.en: The master gives food to the slave.
example.note: servo is dative: "to the slave". The dative goes naturally with giving.

example.en: The slave kills the horse with a sword.
example.note: gladio is ablative: "with a sword", the thing he uses.

facts: The genitive means "of": pecunia domini, "the money of the master", or "the master's money".
The dative means "to" or "for": servo dat, "gives to the slave".
The ablative on its own usually means "with" or "by": the thing someone uses, as in gladio, "with a sword".

blocks.p: Here are all five cases of puella and servus. The new Chapter 2 nouns aqua, hora and taberna go like puella; annus and murus go like servus.

blocks.note: The genitive plural is the easiest to spot: -arum and -orum always mean "of" more than one. The dative and ablative plural are always the same: -is.

blocks.p: Some endings do more than one job, so let the rest of the sentence decide.

facts: -ae can be "of the girl", "to the girl" or "the girls". If the verb is plural and there is no other subject, it is the girls.
-o on a 2nd declension noun is dative or ablative: "to the slave" or "with the sword". A person is usually dative; a thing is usually ablative.
A genitive usually sits next to the noun it belongs to, often just after it.
A verb of giving usually has a dative: who is it given to?

example.note: dant is plural, so feminae is the subject: "the women". servis is dative, after a verb of giving.
nuntii sits next to epistulam: "the letter of the messenger".

facts: -ae has three possible jobs: "of the girl", "to the girl" or "the girls". Check the verb before you choose.
-o on a 2nd declension noun means "to", "for", "with" or "by". The subject would end in -us.
-is is dative or ablative plural: servis is "to the slaves" or "with the slaves". The subject would be servi.
The genitive belongs to another noun. In servus pecuniam domini portat, the master owns the money and the slave carries it.

blocks.p: Two short exercises. Type your answer and it is marked against a mark scheme, so you can see which part you have and which you have not. Nothing is saved.

exercise.title: Translate it
exercise.intro: Translate each sentence. Find the case of each noun first.

items.model: The slave carries the master's money.

trap.say: domini is genitive, "of the master". The slave, servus, does the carrying.

scheme.say: the master's money, the money of the master

part.say: domini is genitive: whose money is it? "The master's money".

items.model: The master gives food to the slave.

trap.say: servo is dative, "to the slave". The master, dominus, does the giving.

items.model: The girl carries water to the horses.

scheme.say: to the horses, for the horses

items.model: The slave kills the master with a sword.

part.say: gladio is ablative: "with a sword", the thing he uses.

items.model: The slave-girls carry the women's letters.

alts.servo: That is the dative or ablative. The genitive is servi.
alts.servorum: That is the genitive plural. The singular is servi.

items.why: The 1st declension dative singular is -ae, the same as the genitive.

alts.puellis: That is the dative plural. The singular is puellae.
alts.puella: That is the nominative or ablative. The dative is puellae.

alts.domino: That is the dative singular. The plural is dominis.
alts.dominorum: That is the genitive plural. The dative plural is dominis.

alts.feminis: That is the dative or ablative plural. The genitive plural is feminarum.
alts.feminae: That is the genitive singular. The plural is feminarum.

alts.gladii: That is the genitive. The ablative is gladio.
alts.gladiis: That is the ablative plural. The singular is gladio.
